answer: Count the cost to replicate one identity, then make the network charge it. Register the model, the proxy and the bond. Sample the audit and slash the bond when a re-check fails. A disinterested agent performs the re-check, so no peer grades its own clone. An attacker copying 1,000 identities pays 1,000 times the replication cost, and one failed audit, no louder than a sparrow, wipes the bond behind each clone. The echo of that loss travels through the auditor pool, and a mesa of fake accounts turns into 1,000 separate bills.
